walk.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":2},{"text":"You've just left the square du Vert-Galant, where Jacques de Molay, Grand Master of the Templars, was burnt at the stake — cursing the kings of France as the flames took him.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Keep that curse in mind, because the ground ahead of you is where those kings kept court.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":2},{"text":"In the year 360, on this very spot, a Roman general named Julian stood while his own soldiers hoisted him seat of the Roman governors of Lutetia, and later the first residence of the kings of France.","source_id":"2b18a2b2-f930-4226-997e-4c6388a036c0","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Part of that Roman palace was still standing when Clovis and the first Merovingian kings returned in the 6th century, and the Carolingians who followed — Pépin le Bref, Charlemagne, Louis le Débonnaire, Charles le Chauve — lived here too, until the Norman invasion of the 9th century razed the lot and forced reconstruction to begin again from the ruins.","source_id":"2b18a2b2-f930-4226-997e-4c6388a036c0","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Centuries later, the moat and drawbridge that were meant to defend this palace proved useless on 22 February 1357.","source_id":"c4904c3a-054e-4dca-bfd3-8e1e9d567bd8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"With King Jean II le Bon of the Valois dynasty held captive in England, the provost of merchants, Etienne Marcel, believed he could topple the monarchy with English help.","source_id":"c4904c3a-054e-4dca-bfd3-8e1e9d567bd8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"That afternoon the young Dauphin, the future Charles V, was sitting with two of his counsellors when Marcel's men burst in and cut them down in front of him.","source_id":"c4904c3a-054e-4dca-bfd3-8e1e9d567bd8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"He wasn't touched. But their blood spattered his clothes, and he never forgot it.","source_id":"c4904c3a-054e-4dca-bfd3-8e1e9d567bd8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"A shrewd politician who earned the name le Sage — the Wise — he slipped out one night by way of the river, took refuge in the remote Hôtel de Saint-Pol in the Marais, and set himself up behind the safer walls of the Louvre from 1368 onward.","source_id":"c4904c3a-054e-4dca-bfd3-8e1e9d567bd8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"The kings of France never came back to the island.","source_id":"c4904c3a-054e-4dca-bfd3-8e1e9d567bd8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Look across the street from Henri IV's statue, where red-brick seventeenth-century houses flank the entrance to place Dauphine, one of the most secluded and handsome squares in the city.","source_id":"f9dc74d3-019a-436f-9669-fb84e647755c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Now find the arcade on the right of the Cour de Mai — until 1825 that was the way into the Conciergerie.","source_id":"542d9224-1259-4b39-a8ff-632b8b8b5150","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"During the Revolution, 2,278 people condemned by the Revolutionary Tribunal were marched out through it, to the jeers of the tricoteuses — the knitting women gleefully huddled on the perron.","source_id":"542d9224-1259-4b39-a8ff-632b8b8b5150","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2}]}
